html:
Usama ibn Munqidh was a Syrian Arab nobleman from Shaizar, a soldier and a poet. Around 1140 he served the ruler of Damascus and often visited Jerusalem, which the Crusaders had held since 1099. The Templars had made the Aqsa Mosque their headquarters. Muslims there pray facing south, towards Mecca. He wrote his memoirs in old age, in the 1180s.

Whenever I visited Jerusalem I always entered the Aqṣa Mosque, beside which stood a small mosque which the Franks had converted into a church. When I used to enter the Aqṣa Mosque, which was occupied by the Templars [al-dāwiyyah], who were my friends, the Templars would evacuate the little adjoining mosque so that I might pray in it.
One day I entered this mosque, repeated the first formula, “Allah is great,” and stood up in the act of praying, upon which one of the Franks rushed on me, got hold of me and turned my face eastward saying, “This is the way thou shouldst pray!” A group of Templars hastened to him, seized him and repelled him from me. I resumed my prayer. … They apologized to me, saying, “This is a stranger who has only recently arrived from the land of the Franks and he has never before seen anyone praying except eastward.” Thereupon I said to myself, “I have had enough prayer.”
